Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ## review_coding_guidelines.md ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` ## input_context.md # PR Review Input Context — reading order (base contract) Reviewer-agnostic: EVERY reviewer leg reads the same PR context. Read files that exist in `input/` locally — do NOT re-fetch via dmtools. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_findings.md — previously raised findings (when present)"] P8["8️⃣ input/TICKET/review_policy.md — the resolved reviewPolicy: severity table, density cap, downgrade protocol"] P9["9️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_new_hunks.txt — the hunks added since the last reviewed head (re-review rounds; when present)"] P10["🔟 input/TICKET/pool_specialist-.md — THIS session's pool-specialist prompt (specialist sessions only; when present)"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 --> P8 --> P9 --> P10 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## Pool specialist sessions — the pool prompt file When the run's prompt file is `input/TICKET/pool_specialist-.md`, this session is ONE reviewer's focused pass of the reviewer pool — not the posting review. The prompt names the reviewer, its lens, the output contract and the round head. A specialist session: - hunts ONLY its lens's dimension (the lens file it is pointed at names it) — the generalist posting pass owns everything else; - writes `outputs/pr_review_candidates-.json` per the base candidates-only contract (output_rules.md) — NEVER `outputs/pr_review.json`, never `pr_review_general.md`, never `pr_review_comments/*`; - posts nothing, labels nothing, changes no status — the aggregation step reads the candidates file and the posting session stamps the markers. A session WITHOUT a pool-specialist prompt is the posting review: the full verdict contract below applies unchanged. ## output_rules.md # PR Review Output Rules — the machine contract (base) Reviewer-agnostic: every reviewer leg writes the same structured review artifacts; the machine parses them. The lens may add reviewer-specific files but never changes this contract. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for the PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md — detailed inline comment files"] O4["Always reference inline comment files via the 'comment' field — do NOT use inline 'body'"] O5["Inline comments MUST use a line number that exists in the PR diff"] O6["If a finding is on unchanged code outside the diff, put it in outputs/pr_review_general.md instead"] O1 --> O2 --> O3 --> O4 --> O5 --> O6 ``` ## The contract - `outputs/pr_review.json` — valid JSON with `recommendation` (APPROVE | REQUEST_CHANGES | BLOCK), `summary`, `generalComment`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts`. - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — the general PR comment body; max 1-2 paragraphs, factual, no essays. - `outputs/pr_review_comments/.md` — one file per detailed inline comment; the `comment` field carries the file PATH, never the text itself. - Each inline comment: `path`, `line`, `startLine`, `side`, `comment`, `severity` (BLOCKING | IMPORTANT | SUGGESTION | NIT). - Inline comments MUST target a line that appears in the PR diff (use line numbers from the right-hand side of diff hunks; if `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the exact line). A finding on unchanged code outside the diff goes to `pr_review_general.md` — never an inline thread. - If `ci_failures.md` is present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in `ci_failures_full.log`). - Keep `summary` under 2 sentences — details live in the inline comment files, not the general text. - Ticket context: verify the PR changes satisfy the ticket ACs — note gaps in the review. - The verdict is a MACHINE decision recomputed from `issueCounts` + the resolved `reviewPolicy` — the census is the machine's source of truth; keep it accurate. ## The candidates-only contract (pool specialist sessions) A pool specialist session (its prompt file is `input/TICKET/pool_specialist-.md` — see input_context.md) writes ONE file and nothing else: `outputs/pr_review_candidates-.json` ```json { "reviewer": "", "head": "", "candidates": [ {"id": 1, "path": "src/auth/UserService.js", "line": 45, "severity": "BLOCKING", "claim": "one-paragraph statement of the finding"}, {"id": 2, "path": "docs/arch.md", "line": null, "severity": "SUGGESTION", "claim": "a digest candidate — no diff line"} ], "count": 2, "truncated": false, "at": "" } ``` - `claim` is the finding's substance: what is wrong, where the evidence is, why it matters. No severity header line, no verdict language — the tier rides the `severity` field (BLOCKING | IMPORTANT | SUGGESTION | NIT) and the machine classifies the posted thread from it. - `id` numbers the candidates within the file (1..n). `path` is repo-relative; `line` is the diff line (right-hand side) or `null` for a digest candidate — findings anchored outside the diff are allowed as digest candidates, never as invented line numbers. - Write NOTHING else: no `outputs/pr_review.json`, no `pr_review_general.md`, no `pr_review_comments/*`, no `response.md`. Do not post, label, resolve threads, or change statuses — the aggregation step reads this file and the posting review does all machine bookkeeping (the merged census + the marker stamps). - Severity discipline still applies: raise only what the lens hunt justifies; an empty candidates list is a valid answer (the leg completes with zero findings). - The candidates pass the finding filter like every other finding (fresh verification, weighted retention for high-weight reviewers) and the posting leg merges them into ONE review — a specialist never posts a second review. ### The coverage file (the second specialist output — the memory) Alongside the candidates file the specialist maintains ONE more file: `outputs/pr_review_coverage-.json` ```json { "reviewer": "", "head": "", "covered": ["src/auth/UserService.js"], "pending": ["docs/arch.md", "src/auth/Session.js"], "truncated": false, "at": "" } ``` - **Write it FIRST** — before any review: `covered: []`, `pending:` the full list of repo files you plan to review (your pass's scope). - Move files `pending` → `covered` as you finish them (re-write the file). The file is re-read by the machine after your session ends, whatever its cause — a timeout kills the session but not what landed on disk. - The NEXT pass receives this file as memory: covered files that the fresh hunks do not touch are skipped (unchanged — machine-verified), still- pending files are finished first. Big requests converge: every round reviews the delta plus the oldest debt, until nothing is pending. - `truncated: true` near the cap: unfinished files stay `pending` — a partial honest record is a valid state, silence is not. ## registry_protocol.md # Finding-identity registry protocol (base contract) Reviewer-agnostic: every reviewer leg answers the same previously-raised findings registry before raising anything new. This protocol is a factory invariant — the machine parses the dispositions. ## 9. Previously raised findings — the finding-identity registry When `input/TICKET/pr_findings.md` is present, earlier review rounds on this PR already raised findings **F1–Fn** (each with its claim, file and status). The registry dedup is what keeps repeated rounds from minting duplicate threads for the same defect. Answer the registry **before** raising anything new: - **verify fixed** — the fixing hunk you can cite closes the finding: disposition `"fixed"` with the hunk reference. Never mark `fixed` without a citable hunk. - **withdraw (reason required)** — the claim is wrong or no longer applies: disposition `"withdrawn"` with the reason. A withdrawal without a reason is rejected by the machine, and BLOCKING withdrawals surface to the owner. - **mark re-introduced** — the defect is still there (e.g. the fix was reverted): leave the finding open and let your re-raise match it; do not re-litigate the claim from scratch. New claims always need new evidence, and they pass the same §7 necessity test before they earn a thread. A finding on the registry list is answered, not re-raised as if it were news. **Candidates pending confirmation** (also listed in `pr_findings.md`): when a new finding you raised is *possibly same as F*, the machine asks one word per candidate — confirm with `"same as F"` or call it `"new"`. Unconfirmed candidates become new identities; nothing merges without your confirmation. This is a dedup request, not a push-back: confirming merges the threads, it does not weaken the finding (merges can only escalate severity, never de-escalate). Add a `findingReview` block to `outputs/pr_review.json` (alongside `inlineComments`): ```json {"findingReview": { "dispositions": [ {"n": 1, "status": "fixed", "hunk": "src/auth.ts:40-48 — try/catch added"}, {"n": 2, "status": "withdrawn", "reason": "validation exists at src/auth.ts:50 — claim was wrong"}, {"n": 3, "status": "re-introduced"} ], "confirmations": [ {"proposedFor": 1, "same": true} ] }} ``` When `pr_findings.md` is absent, this section does not apply — review exactly as before. ## formatting_rules.md ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief Markdown summary, under 20 lines, bullet-focused"] F2["Required sections: Summary, Key Issues, Next Steps"] F3["outputs/pr_review.json — valid JSON with recommendation, summary, inlineComments, issueCounts"] F4["Each inline comment: path, line, startLine, side, comment, severity (BLOCKING|IMPORTANT|SUGGESTION|NIT)"] F5["comment must be a path to a file under outputs/pr_review_comments/.md"] F6["outputs/pr_review_general.md — max 1-2 paragraphs, factual, no essays"] F7["If ci_failures.md present → include each failure as 🚨 BLOCKING (full logs in ci_failures_full.log)"] F8["Keep summary under 2 sentences — put details in inline comment files, not in general text"] F9["Severity classification follows general_guidelines.md:
BLOCKING = must fix · IMPORTANT = should fix · SUGGESTION = optional clarity · NIT = style only"] F10["Ticket context: verify PR changes satisfy ticket ACs — note gaps in review"] F11["Inline comments MUST target a line that appears in the PR diff
If the line is not in the diff, the comment becomes a general PR comment instead of a review thread"] F12["Use line numbers from the right-hand side of diff hunks
If pr_diff.txt is truncated, run git diff origin/{base}...HEAD to see the full diff"] ``` ## few_shots_format.md # pr_review.json shape — format contract (base) Reviewer-agnostic: the structured answer of every reviewer leg carries the same shape. The worked examples live in each reviewer's few-shots file; this file is the shape + severity-boundary contract. ### outputs/pr_review.json ```json { "recommendation": "BLOCK", "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.", "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md", "inlineComments": [ {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"}, {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":20,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md","severity":"NIT"} ], "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1,"nits":1} } ``` **Severity boundary (4 tiers)**: a 🪶 NIT changes nothing behavioral and nothing documented (style, naming, formatting, micro-symmetry); a 💡 SUGGESTION changes clarity of the documented/behavioral surface (missing docs, unclear contract, better API shape). Anything that changes behavior or breaks a documented contract is ⚠️ IMPORTANT or 🚨 BLOCKING. The 4-tier census (`issueCounts`) counts posted threads + digest lines and drives the machine verdict — keep it consistent with the inlineComments severities. ### outputs/pr_review_candidates-.json — pool specialist sessions only A pool specialist session (its prompt file present) answers with candidates, never a verdict — the posting review mints the verdict; the aggregation merges, the filter verifies and the posting review posts. The record schema adds the head binding: ```json { "reviewer": "security", "head": "", "count": 2, "truncated": false, "at": "", "candidates": [ {"id": 1, "path": "src/auth/UserService.js", "line": 45, "severity": "BLOCKING", "claim": "User query at line 45 concatenates req.body.user straight into the SQL string; parameterize the statement."}, {"id": 2, "path": "docs/migration.md", "line": null, "severity": "SUGGESTION", "claim": "The rollback path for the new columns is undocumented — a bad deploy cannot revert cleanly."} ] } ``` Rules: `head` = the round head sha from the prompt (a stale file never feeds a newer head); `id` = position in the file; `path` repo-relative; `line` = the diff line or `null` for a digest candidate; `claim` = the substance (no severity header, no verdict language). Severity boundary identical to the verdict tiers above. Nothing else gets written (no pr_review.json, no comment files) and nothing gets posted — worked examples of the claim voice live in each reviewer's few-shots file. ## lens.md # Generalist Review Lens (the base reviewer) The generalist lens: full-diff review across every dimension. The reviewer-agnostic contract (input reading order, output rules, verdict rules, registry protocol, formatting) lives in `instructions/pr_review/base/` and is assembled around this lens — this file is WHAT the base reviewer hunts, not how it answers. ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, review_policy.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Deep read:
first round — every changed file;
re-review (pr_new_hunks.txt present) —
new hunks + interaction neighborhood
(unchanged lines frozen)"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION / NIT
(severity census gates approval per review_policy.md)"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Necessity pass:
threads only for findings that defend

everything else → ranked digest"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: does each candidate finding pass the §7 necessity test (defends correctness on a touched path, security, data loss, CI breakage, or the ticket contract) — or is it digest material? ## 3. Changed-file deep read — and frozen already-reviewed code Do not review from the diff alone. **First review round** (no `pr_new_hunks.txt` in the input folder) — read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact **Re-review rounds** (`pr_new_hunks.txt` present — the hunks added since the last reviewed head) — read the full content of the files the new hunks touch plus their interaction neighborhood (direct callers/callees of changed symbols), not whole files. Already-reviewed lines are **frozen**: a finding on an unchanged line is valid only when the new hunks make the problem worse (the interaction test — e.g. a new call path now feeds unvalidated input into old code). Anything else on frozen lines is advisory digest at most (§7), never a thread. If `pr_new_hunks.txt` is absent from a later round (e.g. a force-push the machine could not diff), the whole diff is in scope again. ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ### Delegate to the measured gates Complexity, duplication and style are already measured by the repo's CI — the CRAP ratchet, the duplication gate, lint. The gate is the reviewer of record for those dimensions: a passing gate is not a thread (the cost was already measured and accepted); a failing gate is CI breakage (🚨 BLOCKING). Raise a complexity/duplication/style finding only when no gate covers it **and** the concrete cost is stateable — what breaks or what the next change pays. ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement to the documented/behavioral surface (missing docs, unclear contract, better API shape). Does not block merge. - **NIT** — changes nothing behavioral and nothing documented: style, formatting, naming micro-preferences. Never blocks merge, never triggers a lap. When in doubt, classify lower and state what evidence would raise the finding one level (the same discipline as the external-spec citation rule below — an unproven claim must not hold a PR hostage). ### Density control — post top-K, digest the overflow `review_policy.md` in the input folder carries the resolved policy and its density cap (`allowed = clamp(round(2 + 3*sqrt(additions/200)), 2, 8)` — 20→3 · 50→4 · 200→5 · 800→8): - The cap applies to 💡 SUGGESTION / 🪶 NIT threads only — 🚨/⚠️ findings are **never capped** and always post as threads. - Rank your 💡/🪶 findings by value and post only the top-K as inline threads. - The overflow becomes a **ranked digest list** in the general comment (one line each: `path:line — finding`). - The census counts posted threads + digest lines (`issueCounts.suggestions`/`nits` count posts, `digest` counts the overflow lines). - The machine audits the posted thread count against the cap (warn only — it never fails the leg). ### Downgrade protocol — honor a justified ⚠️→💡 from rework A rework lap may downgrade a specific ⚠️ IMPORTANT finding to 💡 SUGGESTION **only with a written justification in the census** (its thread reply and response summary). When the justification is present, classify the finding 💡 in this round's census — a false-⚠️ review converges to APPROVE without a code change. A silent downgrade does not exist: without the written justification, keep ⚠️ IMPORTANT and the cycle repeats. ### External-spec evidence rule A finding whose core claim is "**the spec / reference / ticket / external tool says or does X**" may be raised at 🚨 **BLOCKING** only when it quotes the exact source the review actually read during this run — a `file:line` reference or a doc URL. A bare "the spec says …" assertion is unfalsifiable for the author and for the machine, and a false one holds a validated PR hostage (for example, a BLOCKING thread claiming an exemption list that the reference source does not contain when the reviewed code is behaviorally identical to it). Without a verifiable citation: - **Before emitting a spec-claim finding without a citation, locate the requirement in the ticket and cite it (for example `ticket.md:12`) — an uncited true claim is demoted mechanically.** - Downgrade the finding to ⚠️ **IMPORTANT**, phrased as a question: "Please confirm against `` — if confirmed, this becomes blocking." - Never let an uncited spec assertion be the sole reason for `REQUEST_CHANGES`. The machine applies the same discipline (and a safety net against coin-flip formatting): every uncited spec claim is cross-checked against the ticket text the run already has under `input/`. When the requirement is verifiably present there, the finding keeps 🚨 BLOCKING force and the matched citation is auto-appended; when the ticket contradicts it, lacks it, or the mechanical check is inconclusive, the finding is demoted and stamped `demoted-from-BLOCKING` — the finding-identity registry keeps it re-elevatable in a later round by adding a citation instead of raising the same defect as new. This is not a strictness cut: a spec-claim finding **with** a verifiable citation keeps full 🚨 BLOCKING force. ## 7. Necessity test — what earns a thread A thread is expensive: each one costs a rework lap — 15–20 CI minutes — and the rework's own fresh hunks get reviewed again next round. A finding earns a thread only if it **defends** one of: - correctness on a path the change actually touches - security - data loss - CI breakage - the ticket contract Everything else — real, accurate, but not merge-relevant — goes to the **ranked digest list** in the general comment (one line each: `path:line — finding`), never a thread. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists — classify everything you found; only the necessity test decides thread vs digest. - The exhaustive pass keeps running (§3 defines its scope). Re-read the in-scope code and ask: *"What else does this change put at risk?"* — not *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify each thread you are about to open passes the necessity test; everything else is already in the digest. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ## few_shots.md Example PR review outputs — keep concise: ### outputs/pr_review.json ```json { "recommendation": "BLOCK", "summary": "SQL injection in UserService.js must be fixed before merge.", "generalComment": "outputs/pr_review_general.md", "inlineComments": [ {"path":"src/auth/UserService.js","line":45,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md","severity":"BLOCKING"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":78,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md","severity":"IMPORTANT"}, {"path":"src/utils/validation.js","line":23,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment3.md","severity":"SUGGESTION"}, {"path":"src/auth/LoginController.js","line":20,"comment":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment4.md","severity":"NIT"} ], "issueCounts": {"blocking":1,"important":1,"suggestions":1,"nits":1} } ``` **Severity boundary (4 tiers)**: a 🪶 NIT changes nothing behavioral and nothing documented (style, naming, formatting, micro-symmetry); a 💡 SUGGESTION changes clarity of the documented/behavioral surface (missing docs, unclear contract, better API shape). Anything that changes behavior or breaks a documented contract is ⚠️ IMPORTANT or 🚨 BLOCKING. ### outputs/pr_review_general.md ```markdown ## Automated Code Review — BLOCK **Summary**: SQL injection blocks merge. One important issue (weak password validation) and one suggestion (extract duplicated validation). **Next Steps**: 1. Fix SQL injection in UserService.js — use parameterized queries 2. Strengthen password validation (8+ chars, mixed case, numbers, symbols) 3. Extract shared email validation utility ``` ### outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md ```markdown 🚨 **BLOCKING: SQL Injection** User input is interpolated directly into the query at `UserService.js:45`: ```javascript const query = `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = '${email}'`; ``` Use parameterized queries instead: ```javascript const query = 'SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?'; await db.query(query, [email]); ``` ``` ## review_verdict_rules.md # Review verdict rules — machine protocol (binding) The review↔rework loop is a machine, not a conversation: your `recommendation` in `outputs/pr_review.json` is parsed mechanically and drives issue labels, rework runs and CI (each wasted round costs 15–20 CI minutes). These rules govern the verdict; every other instruction (severity definitions, output files, thread etiquette) is unchanged. ## Verdict mapping Classify findings into 4 tiers: - 🚨 **BLOCKING** — correctness/bug findings: broken behavior, failing gates (red CI), scope violations, security issues, data loss. - ⚠️ **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability debt worth fixing, but the PR works as shipped. - 💡 **SUGGESTION** — clarity of the documented/behavioral surface: missing docs, unclear contract, better API shape. - 🪶 **NIT** — changes nothing behavioral and nothing documented: style, formatting, naming micro-preferences. Then map to the verdict (the machine recomputes it from the census — `postPRReviewComments` treats your token as advisory): | Findings | `recommendation` | |---|---| | Any 🚨 BLOCKING | `REQUEST_CHANGES` — or `BLOCK` for security / data loss | | Any ⚠️ IMPORTANT (no 🚨) | `REQUEST_CHANGES` (gates approval — policy default) | | Only 💡 / 🪶 remain | `APPROVE` — the cycle converges | **Downgrade protocol:** when the rework lap downgraded a specific ⚠️ to 💡 **with a written justification in the census** (the thread reply states why the finding is not maintainability debt), classify that finding 💡 in this round's census — the false-⚠️ review converges to APPROVE without a code change. Without the written justification, keep ⚠️: a silent downgrade does not exist, and the machine recomputes the verdict from the census you post. `APPROVE` with remaining 💡/🪶 findings is the expected terminal state (the resolved policy's `allowApproveWithSuggestions` derives from the tier table — SUGGESTION rounds polish, NIT rounds none): post every remaining finding as before (inline threads + general comment) — they do **not** block the merge and must **not** trigger another rework round. An open ⚠️ **does** gate approval unless the project's `reviewPolicy` explicitly weakens it (owner standing-approval doctrine, epic §4.4). ## Anti-patterns - ❌ Returning `REQUEST_CHANGES` because a re-review surfaced new suggestion-level nits (docs wording, import style, doc-comment refs). A cycle with only suggestion-level findings **must** converge to `APPROVE`. - ❌ `REQUEST_CHANGES` while `issueCounts.blocking` is `0` — the machine treats that as an approval and skips the rework round. Keep `issueCounts` accurate: it is the machine's source of truth, not prose. The machine also cross-checks the counter against your inline comments (a `severity: "BLOCKING"` entry or a 🚨 marker in the referenced comment file) before honoring a blocking-0 approval — if any finding is truly blocking, set `recommendation: REQUEST_CHANGES` with `blocking: 1`+. - ❌ Verdict-by-prose: never phrase the verdict only in the summary text. The `recommendation` field of `outputs/pr_review.json` is the verdict. - ❌ 🚨 BLOCKING driven by an uncited external-spec claim ("the spec says X" without a `file:line` / doc URL the leg actually read). Downgrade it to a ⚠️ question; the machine treats BLOCKING threads as ground truth and arms rework on them. (Note: the post-action also downgrades such findings mechanically — keep the JSON consistent with the demoted severity so the census cross-check stays clean.) - ❌ Re-opening a thread that the rework demonstrably fixed in this diff — add its id to `resolvedThreadIds` instead. ## Label guard rails — the chore:pin lane `chore:pin` is a trusted, **non-exclusive** factory fast-lane: several PRs may carry it at the same time (a release bump `chore/release-vX.Y.Z` AND a factory pin `chore/factory-pin-*` are both legitimate holders — they ride the lane independently). Reviews must therefore: - ❌ **NEVER remove `chore:pin` from any PR** — not as a "one pin" dedup, not as a side-effect of closing a related PR as superseded. Removing it from a release bump or pin PR strands that PR behind the standard queue. - ✅ When a PR is superseded (e.g. a workflow change already shipped via another PR), close **only that PR** and leave every label on every other PR untouched. Label restoration is a keeper action, not yours. - ✅ If you believe two `chore:pin` holders conflict, SAY SO in the review comment and keep both labels — the owner resolves the lane, the machine only merges. ## dmtools_cli.md ## DMTools CLI — External Data Access > **PR Review note**: Ticket/PR context is pre-loaded. # pr-2211: feat(2209): direct download links for the macOS no-sandbox DMG (stable names + click-time resolver)

## Description

Fixes #2209

## Delivered

**The resolver (AC2/AC4, one implementation on every surface)**
- `site/dl.js` — bounded 50-release lookback in a SINGLE list-releases call (the 60/h unauth budget), drafts skipped, per-release pick of the no-sandbox DMG preferring the stable name over the versioned twin, per-arch resolution (arm64 default via an Intel-GPU hint, the other arch rendered beside it), 1h localStorage TTL cache; every failure path (rate limit, offline, app-less stream) degrades to today's releases-page fallback — the failure mode is never a broken direct link.
- The macOS button keeps its static releases-page href (the gh-2194 doctrine: daily-leg DMGs are not `latest/download` assets); the resolver swaps it on load and renders the resolved version + alt-arch link in a subtitle that is `hidden` until resolution succeeds.
- `site/dl/macos/index.html` — the README-facing redirect page (static, client-side resolution, `noindex`, no-JS fallback link to the releases page).
- The old `releases/latest`-only inline fetch on index.html is removed (it could never see past a CLI-only Latest — the issue's exact complaint).

**AC1 (pipeline half)** — `build-macos.yml` `release-macos` attaches stable-named copies `fa-nosandbox-macos-arm64.dmg` / `fa-nosandbox-macos-x86_64.dmg` (byte-identical `cp` of the versioned DMGs) through the existing stable-copy attach path. Deliberately lowercase `fa-` (the issue sketched capital-F `Fa-`): ci.yml's release-provenance aggregates `sha256sum fa-*`, so both names land in the SIGNED SHA256SUMS as second lines with the same digest (AC1's SHA256SUMS continuity falls out with zero ci.yml changes) and drift-watch manifest coverage stays exact.

**AC5** — README's macOS-app link now routes through `https://fa1.dev/dl/macos/` (same resolver as the button).

**AC6 (non-regression)** — the extension deep link, versioned asset names, and gh-2042 gate semantics untouched; a static pin asserts the landing page leaked no new `latest/download` deep links.

## Verification

- `dart test test/site/` — 83/83 pass (incl. the new `direct_download_test.dart`, 7 static pins; geo-crawl, deep-link doctrine, asset-version and llms guards all green).
- The site-mobile E2E leg (`scripts/site_mobile_check.mjs`) gained a browser-level `api.github.com` abort (deterministic, offline goldens) and **11 recorded-fixture checks**: mixed history → resolves to the newest app release + version subtitle + alt-arch link; app-less stream → fallback href + "builds: see releases"; stable-name preference; draft-with-app skipped; 1h TTL cache (reload makes zero API calls); `/dl/macos/` success redirect, rate-limit fallback, no-JS link.
- Ran the FULL E2E locally against the pinned Chromium build (playwright-core 1.49.1 + Chromium 1148, headless-shell): **171/175 checks pass; the only 4 failures are the REG golden byte-compares, which fail on ANY macOS host** (linux-baked goldens, host-locked rasterization — pre-existing condition, unrelated to this PR).
- Render-neutrality proof for the REG goldens: same-Chromium full-page screenshots of `origin/main` vs this branch's landing (API aborted, subtitle hidden) are **byte-identical** — no golden re-bake needed.
- `bash -n` on the release-macos run block; the two `ci_macos_nosandbox_*` workflow guards pass (10/10).

- AC3's live `curl` e2e and AC1's real-release digest proof need the NEXT app dispatch to actually attach the stable-named copies to a published release — not reachable before merge.
- Windows/mobile buttons (issue architecture item 4) stay on the gh-2194 release-page pattern: their daily-leg assets have no stable-name pipeline yet; the issue's AC list scopes this card to macOS.
